generated_video_script.full_script:
[INÍCIO DO ROTEIRO - 7.331 caracteres]

Hippocrates, the father of medicine, built his first hospital next to a stream.

He grew a specific plant in that water. He used it to treat his patients.

The Persian king Xerxes ordered his entire army to eat it during long marches. The Romans sold it in regulated markets as pharmaceutical-grade food. The Japanese still eat it as a New Year ritual.

In 2014, the United States Centers for Disease Control ranked it as the most nutrient-dense food on Earth. The only one, out of 47 foods tested, to score a perfect 100.

What is this plant?

It's duckweed.

Yes, the plant that covers ponds and is considered a weed is actually the most nutritious food on the planet.

It has more omega-3 than salmon. More protein than soy. And it can be grown anywhere with standing water.

So why don't we eat it?

Because it can't be patented. Because it's free. Because it grows anywhere.

And unfortunately, in today's world, what is free is often forgotten.

But it doesn't have to be. Nature Lost Vault is here to rediscover these secrets.

Subscribe so you don't miss the next episodes.

[FIM DO ROTEIRO - 7.331 caracteres]
